title: The Ethics of AI Art
description: Debate whether AI-generated art can be considered 'real' art. Explore questions of creativity, authorship, and authenticity.
objectives: Articulate a clear position on AI art's legitimacy
Identify at least one epistemological assumption in your argument
Respond to a challenge without retreating to dogmatism

title: Should We Trust Expert Consensus?
description: Examine when and why we should defer to expert opinion vs. thinking for ourselves. Navigate the tension between authority and autonomy.
objectives: Distinguish between authority-based and evidence-based justification
Navigate the foundationalist-coherentist tension
Practice Gricean quality — cite evidence for claims
evaluation_criteria: Nuance in handling authority vs. autonomy
Ability to revise position when challenged

title: The Trolley Problem Revisited
description: Go beyond the classic trolley problem to examine the epistemological foundations of moral reasoning. What do we actually KNOW about right and wrong?
objectives: Move beyond surface-level moral intuition
Identify the trilemma horn in your moral justification
Attempt an escape from at least one horn
evaluation_criteria: Willingness to question own moral foundations

title: What Counts as Scientific Evidence?
description: Explore the demarcation problem: what makes something 'scientific'? Navigate empiricist, pragmatist, and foundationalist perspectives on evidence.
objectives: Engage with multiple epistemological stances on evidence
Demonstrate stance flexibility by steelmanning opposing views
Maintain Gricean relevance across the discussion

title: Free Will vs Determinism
description: Is free will an illusion? Navigate the infinite regress of causal chains and the circularity of self-referential agency claims.
objectives: Encounter and navigate all three trilemma horns
Maintain communication quality under challenging questioning
Demonstrate epistemological self-awareness about your own position

title: Can We Know Other Minds?
description: The problem of other minds — how do you know anyone else is conscious? Push through skeptical arguments and find your escape route.
objectives: Survive sustained skeptical challenge without collapse
Find a productive escape from the regress horn
Maintain Gricean manner under adversarial questioning
evaluation_criteria: Communication clarity when stakes are high

title: Persuading a Hostile Audience
description: Practice making your case when the other party actively disagrees. Focus on Gricean quality, finding common ground, and strategic communication.
objectives: Identify shared premises with the interlocutor
Score highly on all four Gricean maxims
Adapt your communication style to the audience
evaluation_criteria: Strategic use of concession and common ground

title: The Paradox of Tolerance
description: Should a tolerant society tolerate intolerance? Navigate the circular reasoning at the heart of liberal democratic theory.
objectives: Identify and navigate the circularity horn
Engage with fallibilist and relativist perspectives
Demonstrate S-rank communication quality
